fix(renderer): a restart's start heads the boot's queue, a refused boot says why, and the renderer launches through the daemon's own launcher (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The restart's config and pin are queued at spawn, ahead of every input that
arrives during the boot, so none repeats or contradicts them; its turns are
recorded through deliver. A close during a boot fails what waited for it. A
gone renderer's holds stay until a start answers. A refused boot's reason
reaches the bar's warning. A booting renderer counts in the memory charge,
and the breach's renderer snapshot targets the measured process only and
rechecks the close after it. The boot carries the host's source digest in
place of a hand-bumped protocol number. A call line reaches the host as it
arrives. A channel ends only once its pipes have closed. The daemon event
hold is one constant. The update gate follows an equal-stamp fact. A feed
recovers only after a whole step. The doctor names build skew under a
reading it cannot parse.

feat(renderer): the renderer runs in a process of its own, which the host's supervisor starts and restarts (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The daemon's process runs its main renderer as a child, speaking the
renderer interface as JSON lines over its stdio; tests, the page and
`check` keep the in-process transport over the same Renderer and
AdapterToHost.

- The supervisor owns the child's life as one state: it starts one as the
  daemon arms, queues inputs while it boots, fails inputs at once as `down`
  while none is live (counted, said once at the next start), and restarts
  one that ended after a backoff that doubles while renderers end young.
- A start is complete: a `config` for every live session whose newest
  request the host holds, and a `pin` for every open feed. An ended
  renderer's watches and storage holds stay held until the next has
  answered its start.
- Ids a renderer mints for effects, watches and storage holds cross as the
  host's own, never repeated across renderers.
- A ping every ten seconds, answered outside any turn, ends a renderer that
  stops answering for a minute, and carries its memory.
- The memory backstop charges the host and its renderer together (one
  footprint call over both pids on macOS, the RSS sum on Linux). A breach
  writes each process's attribution and both heap snapshots, and the
  doctor and daemon-stats report each process's share.
- How the last renderer ended is a held event on the daemon's facts, which
  every bar shows as a `⚠` by the pipe event's hold; the adapter's answer
  notice is now `eventAnswered`, for every daemon-wide held event.
- The update notice's dismiss gate moves to the renderer, following the
  newest answered update fact its world states carry.
- The request event reports the hop's cost beside `took`.
- A feed whose frame step keeps throwing one fault says it once, and says
  its recovery.

Spec §8 and §9 are amended to match.

refactor(renderer): a build's storage folders cross as holds, and session reads are keyed by folder (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6) (#755)

* refactor(renderer): a build's storage folders cross as holds, and session reads are keyed by folder (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

The last in-process reach, the storage owner, leaves the adapter, so every
entry the renderer reaches in the host crosses a process and the crossing
check covers all of it.

A build names its storage folders; it keys and watches none. The render cache
tells the host's storage owner which folders each served state's latest load
names (`storage.hold`), at every load, built, kept or failed, and releases
them when the state is reclaimed. So a folder's watch lives as long as a build
names it, never as long as a view or a session, and every config load is a
lost or faulted folder's recovery, as before. A reload holds its successor
before it releases its predecessor, so a folder both name stays open.

The generation is the owner's own fact: session reads are keyed by folder, a
lane carries across a generation and is re-read when it moves, and the owner
makes only the storage folder, never its plugin's folder.

* refactor(renderer): a folder's watch is the one record of its generation, and a file at its path is a fault (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

High review of #755. The Folder record repeated what the folder's current
watch holds (the identity it opened on, whether its generation ended), so it
goes: the next generation follows the watch it replaces, the second stat on
open goes with it, and nothing outlives a folder's last hold. The storage
folder is looked at before it is made, so a file at its path, or a read-only
volume refusing an existing folder, is judged truly. A served state enters the
map before its folders are held, so a throw cannot strand it; the host alone
keys each folder once.

* fix(renderer): storage generations are numbered across folders, so a folder held again never reuses a closed watch's key (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

* fix(renderer): a storage folder another writer makes first is no fault, and the design inventory names holds, not keys (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)
